changes.before: In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage‑backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals.
changes.after: Last December, the Committee indicated that it would continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage‑backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward its maximum employment and price stability goals. Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals, and the Committee will continue to assess progress in coming meetings.

changes.before: Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.
changes.after: With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen.

changes.before: The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak but have shown improvement.
changes.after: The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have shown improvement but have not fully recovered.

changes.before: The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus.
changes.after: The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus.

changes.before: Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.

parsed.rationale: The statement says the economy has made progress toward the asset-purchase taper criterion and that the Committee will assess progress in coming meetings, which signals that a taper is approaching. The economic assessment is also somewhat more upbeat, while rate guidance is unchanged.

spans.quote: In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage‑backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals.
Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.
The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak but have shown improvement.
The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus.
Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.

Last December, the Committee indicated that it would continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage‑backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward its maximum employment and price stability goals. Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals, and the Committee will continue to assess progress in coming meetings.
With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen.
The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have shown improvement but have not fully recovered.
The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus.
